issues.t: Valve cover oil leak kills alternator and can stall engine (recall)
issues.sym: Burning oil smell, oil on the alternator, a battery or charging light, dimming lights, and in bad cases the engine losing power or stalling while driving.
issues.why: Oil leaks from the front valve cover gasket and drips onto the alternator below it, which can disable the charging system. Hyundai recalled every Veracruz, then reopened the campaign in 2020 because some repaired cars leaked again.
issues.next: If the battery light comes on, get off the road safely, because the car may stall once the battery runs down. Check your VIN for recalls 14V-415 and 20V-705; the gasket and alternator repair is free.

issues.t: Rear valve cover and spark plug tube seal leaks
issues.sym: Oil seeping around the rear valve cover, a burning oil smell after driving, or oil in the spark plug wells causing a misfire.
issues.why: Beyond the recalled front cover, the rear valve cover gasket and spark plug tube seals also harden and leak, and owners report repeat leaks after earlier repairs.
issues.next: Have both valve covers checked when one is resealed. Oil in the plug wells can ruin ignition coils, so fix it early.

issues.sym: Oil seeping from the front of the engine behind the drive belts, drops under the front of the vehicle, or oil reaching the alternator.
issues.why: The front timing cover seal leaks with age. It is a big job, around 10 hours, because much of the front of the engine comes apart.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the oil level. A light seep can be watched; fix it if it drips steadily or reaches belts and electrical parts.

issues.sym: Oil spots under the engine and a low oil level between changes.
issues.why: The oil pan sealant and gasket leak as the vehicle ages.
issues.next: Check the oil level regularly and have the pan resealed if spots keep appearing.

issues.t: Surging, sputtering or limp mode from throttle problems
issues.sym: Surging at steady speeds, sputtering like it is starving for fuel, little or no response from the gas pedal, the vehicle stuck at low speed, and a check engine light.
issues.why: The throttle position sensor or the electronic throttle body fails. Fixes often include a new sensor or throttle body and an engine computer update, though a few owners had symptoms return.
issues.next: Have the codes read right away and pull over safely if power drops. Ask the dealer about engine computer updates with the throttle repair.

issues.sym: Hard or clunky shifts, a delay before gears engage, or engine revs flaring as if the transmission slipped.
issues.why: RepairPal reports harsh shifting and slipping on the 6-speed automatic across all years.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and condition, and ask a dealer about software updates before replacing parts. Get it checked quickly if it slips.

issues.t: ABS and stability control lights come on randomly
issues.sym: The ABS, ESC and brake warning lights flicker on and off or stay on, with wheel speed sensor or brake module codes.
issues.why: Owners have traced it to failed rear wheel speed sensors or, less often, a failed ABS/ESC hydraulic module. One owner was quoted for a module when the sensors were the real problem.
issues.next: Get the ABS codes read. Test the wheel speed sensors before agreeing to replace the expensive module.

issues.t: ABS module can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. Some owners notice the ABS light, a burning smell or smoke from the engine bay, even when parked.
issues.why: Brake fluid can leak inside the ABS module and cause a short circuit, which can start an engine compartment fire.
issues.next: Park outside and away from buildings until the fix is done. Check your VIN for recall 23V-651.

issues.sym: Brake lights stay off or stay on, cruise control does not cancel when braking, the stability control light comes on, or the shifter can leave Park without the brake.
issues.why: The brake light switch can fail. Hyundai recalled it on 2007-2008 and 2008-2011 models.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights. Check your VIN for recalls 09V-122 and 13V-113.

issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on, and the horn or steering wheel buttons may act up.
issues.why: Resistance can build up in the clock spring, the coiled connector behind the steering wheel, which can stop the driver airbag from deploying.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 11V-472; the clock spring is replaced for free.

issues.sym: A burning smell or melted wiring near the trailer hitch harness, or trailer lights that stop working.
issues.why: Moisture can get into the circuit board of certain dealer-installed Thule (2007-2008) and aftermarket CURT (2009-2011) tow wiring modules, which can short and overheat.
issues.next: If you have a factory or dealer tow package, check your VIN for recall 08E-055; CURT harness owners should check recall 11E-041.

issues.sym: The wipers work on and off, then stop completely, sometimes in the middle of a storm.
issues.why: The wiper motor or its linkage fails.
issues.next: Do not drive in rain or snow without working wipers. Have the motor and linkage replaced.

issues.t: Key fob stops locking and unlocking doors
issues.sym: The remote no longer locks or unlocks the doors even with a new battery.
issues.why: Owners report failures in the keyless entry system, with average repair bills around $1,700.
issues.next: Try a new fob battery and the spare fob first. If neither works, have the keyless entry receiver and module tested before buying new fobs.

issues.sym: An inside door handle snaps or comes loose, so the door will not open from inside.
issues.why: The interior handle or its mounting cracks with use.
issues.next: Use another door until fixed. The handle is a simple replacement part.

issues.t: Engine shuts off or fails at highway speed
issues.sym: The engine cuts out suddenly at highway speed, sometimes after earlier oil leak repairs, and in some cases the engine fails completely.
issues.why: Owners report total engine failures at high mileage and stalls after valve cover oil leak repairs. Oil reaching the alternator can also make the engine die when the battery runs flat.
issues.next: Make sure the valve cover recall has been done and the charging system works. If the engine knocks or will not restart, have it towed rather than driven.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle at high mileage
issues.sym: A rattle from the front of the engine on start-up or at idle, sometimes with cam timing codes.
issues.why: The timing chains, tensioners and guides wear, and oil-soaked parts from long-term leaks add to the wear.
issues.next: Do not wait if the rattle gets louder. Have the timing system inspected before a chain jumps and damages the engine.

issues.t: Check engine light from oxygen sensor
issues.sym: Check engine light, sometimes with chugging around 30-35 mph or a rough idle.
issues.why: Upstream and downstream oxygen sensors fail on these vehicles, according to owner repair records.
issues.next: Have the codes read and replace the sensor the code points to.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning light stays on
issues.sym: The TPMS light comes on or flashes even when the tires are properly inflated.
issues.why: A tire pressure sensor or its battery fails, or a sensor was not registered after a tire change.
issues.next: Check all tire pressures, including the spare if it has a sensor. If the light stays on, have the sensors scanned.
